newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REPORT YANKEES TO CONTINUE FIGHT FOR IRABU.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REPORT YANKEES TO CONTINUE FIGHT FOR IRABU.

text.p: The New York Yankees are planning to carry on the fight for star Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu by filing a grievance to protest a ruling that gave the San Diego Padres exclusive negotiating rights to him, a published report said Friday.
"The fight hasn't begun yet," Yankees owner George Steinbrenner told the New York Post over the battle for Irabu. "There hasn't been a grievance filed yet. We will do that."

A four-member committee formed to investigate the controversy surrounding Irabu's status, recommended that his major league rights belonged to the Padres as the result of a working agreement between the National League team and Irabu's Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines.
Irabu, however, has stated numerous times that the only major league team with whom he is willing to play for is the Yankees.
Steinbrenner originally challenged the working agreement between the Padres and Chiba Lotte and apparently is not willing to accept the recommendation of the Executive Council.
"The young man should have a chance to play ball where he wants," Steinbrenner told the newspaper. "You know the Yankees always have to battle. A lot of guys are jealous."
But a trade appears to be the only way the Yankees could land the hard-throwing Irabu.
Irabu was 12-6 last season and led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA.
